{"body":"## Summary

- **`worktreeStatus(path)`** (`src/lib/workflow/worktree-manager.ts`) returns `"clean"`, `"dirty"` or `"unknown"`. It is now the only place in `src/lib/workflow` that runs `git status --porcelain` to decide whether a worktree is dirty. It replaces both `isWorktreeDirty` copies and the freshness check's own call. It returns `unknown` when git cannot run or exits non-zero.
- **Each caller keeps its existing behaviour for `unknown`:**
  - Signal-shutdown cleanup still keeps the worktree, but the log now says `preserved (worktree status unreadable)` instead of claiming uncommitted changes. This check runs before the commits-ahead check, which would otherwise mislabel the reason as "commits ahead of base".
  - The chain-resume resolver still treats `unknown` as not dirty.
  - `checkWorktreeFreshness` still treats it as not dirty.
- **`formatSignalLine(issue, pid, result, { indent })`** is now in `src/lib/locks/signal-line.ts` and exported from `src/lib/locks/index.ts`. `sequant locks` calls it with no indent; the orchestrator calls it with two spaces. Each reason has one text. For a stale PID, `sequant run` now prints the longer `sequant locks` wording.
- The hand-written copy of the check in `chain-resume.integration.test.ts` now calls the real `worktreeStatus`.
- The three porcelain parsers named in AC-1 (`-z` checkpoint, `phase-executor.ts`, `qa-stagnation.ts`) are untouched.
